1. **Dignity First:** All services shall be delivered in a manner that respects the inherent dignity and privacy of every guest. No individual shall be turned away from an AESN facility solely due to lack of documentation or identification.

2. **Temporary Bridge:** Shelters operated by the Network are intended as a temporary bridge, typically not exceeding ninety (90) days, during which guests are connected to long-term housing solutions, vocational training, or family reunification services.

3. **Safety and Security:** Every facility shall maintain a secure environment with 24/7 staffing, controlled entry, and a zero-tolerance policy for violence, theft, substance abuse on premises, or harassment.

4. **Non-Refoulement:** No guest shall be forcibly transferred to another facility or returned to a hazardous situation without a documented alternative plan agreed upon by the guest and a case manager.

5. **Transparency:** All financial transactions, donor contributions, and expenditure records shall be maintained in an auditable manner and made available to the Board of Directors and relevant regulatory authorities upon request.

6. **Collaboration:** The Network shall actively coordinate with government bodies, local law enforcement, healthcare providers, and other non-governmental organizations to ensure comprehensive support for guests.

---

**ARTICLE III: GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE**

**Section 3.1: Board of Directors**

The affairs of the Network shall be managed by a Board of Directors comprising not less than five (5) and not more than nine (9) members. The initial Board of Directors, as of 2015-04-01, is constituted as follows:

| Shri Harish Gowda | Member | Retired IPS Officer, Karnataka Cadre |

**Section 3.2: Terms and Meetings**

- Board members shall serve a term of three (3) years, renewable by mutual consent.
- The Board shall convene at least once per quarter. A simple majority shall constitute a quorum.
- Day-to-day operational decisions may be delegated to the Executive Director, who shall report to the Board.

**Section 3.3: Executive Director**

The Executive Director shall be appointed by the Board and shall be responsible for:
- Overseeing all shelter operations and staff.
- Implementing Board policies.
- Managing donor relations and fundraising.
- Ensuring compliance with all applicable local, state, and central regulations.

---

**ARTICLE IV: OPERATIONAL SCOPE**

**Section 4.1: Types of Facilities**

AESN may operate, either directly or in partnership, the following types of facilities:
- **Emergency Night Shelters:** Open year-round, providing overnight accommodation and morning meals.
- **Family Transition Shelters:** Private or semi-private rooms for families with children, with access to communal kitchen and laundry facilities.
- **Disaster Response Camps:** Temporary structures set up in the immediate aftermath of a natural calamity, in coordination with the Karnataka State Disaster Management Authority.
**Section 5.3: Staffing Norms**

- Each emergency night shelter shall have a minimum of two (2) staff members on duty during operational hours.
- A caretaker shall be present on the premises at all times.
- Volunteers may supplement staff, but shall not replace paid positions.
- All staff shall undergo a background verification prior to appointment.

**Section 5.4: Grievance Redressal**

A Grievance Redressal Committee shall be constituted at the headquarters in Mumbai. The Committee shall:
- Receive complaints from beneficiaries, staff, or the public.
- Acknowledge receipt of a complaint within three (3) working days.
- Resolve the complaint within thirty (30) days of receipt.
- Maintain a register of complaints and their resolutions.

---

**ARTICLE VI: FINANCIAL PROVISIONS**

**Section 6.1: Sources of Funding**

The Network may raise funds through:
- Grants from central and state government schemes, including the National Urban Livelihoods Mission and state-level homelessness programs.
- Donations from individuals, trusts, and corporations.
- Corporate social responsibility contributions.
- Income from lawful activities, including the sale of recycled materials.

**Section 6.2: Utilization of Funds**

Funds shall be utilized for:
- Operational expenses, including rent, utilities, and staff salaries.
- Procurement of food, bedding, and hygiene supplies.
- Maintenance and minor repairs of facilities.
- Training and capacity-building of staff.
- Contingency reserves for disaster response.

**Section 6.3: Auditing**

- The accounts of the Network shall be audited annually by a chartered accountant appointed by the Board.
- The audited financial statements shall be presented to the Board within six (6) months of the close of the financial year.
- A copy of the audited statements shall be made available to donors and regulatory authorities upon request.

---

**ARTICLE VII: AMENDMENTS**

According to the administrative records, Aashraya Emergency Shelter Network has headquarters in Mumbai. Record status: current.

**Section 7.1: Procedure for Amendment**

This charter may be amended by a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority of the Board members present and voting, provided that:
- Notice of the proposed amendment is circulated at least fifteen (15) days prior to the meeting.
- The amendment is consistent with the objectives of the Network and applicable law.

**Section 7.2: Record of Amendments**

All amendments shall be recorded in a separate register maintained at the headquarters in Mumbai, with the date of amendment and the names of the Board members voting in favour.

---

**ARTICLE VIII: DISSOLUTION**

**Section 8.1: Dissolution Procedure**

The Network may be dissolved by a resolution passed by a three-fourths majority of the total Board membership. Upon dissolution:
- All debts and liabilities shall be settled.
- Remaining assets shall be transferred to another organization with similar objectives, as decided by the Board.
- A final report shall be submitted to the Registrar of Societies.

---

**Section 8.2: Effective Date**

This charter shall take effect from the date of its adoption, as recorded in the minutes of the founding meeting.

---

**CERTIFICATION**

We, the undersigned, being the founding members of Aashraya Emergency Shelter Network, hereby certify that the above constitutes the true and complete charter of the Network, adopted on this day, 2015-04-01.
**SECTION 9: OPERATIONAL SCOPE AND SERVICE AREAS**

**Section 9.1: Primary Service Areas**

The Network shall operate emergency shelters and allied services within the following administrative regions, subject to the availability of resources and the execution of memoranda of understanding with local authorities:

1. Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR), including the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai, Thane Municipal Corporation, Navi Mumbai Municipal Corporation, and the Panvel Municipal Corporation.
2. Pune Metropolitan Region, including the Pune Municipal Corporation and Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation.
3. Nagpur Municipal Corporation.
4. Nashik Municipal Corporation.
5. Aurangabad Municipal Corporation.
6. Such other districts or municipal areas as the Board may designate by resolution from time to time.

The Board may, upon recommendation of the Executive Director, temporarily extend operations beyond the above areas in response to a declared disaster, a public health emergency, or a mass displacement event, provided that such extension is documented and reported to the Board at its next meeting.

**Section 9.2: Nature of Services**

The Network shall provide, or facilitate through partner agencies, the following categories of services:

1. **Emergency Shelter:** Provision of temporary, safe, and dignified accommodation for individuals and families rendered homeless due to disaster, fire, eviction, domestic violence, or other crises. Shelter facilities shall be operated on a twenty-four-hour basis and shall include separate dormitories for men, women, and families, with due regard for privacy and safety.
2. **Food and Nutrition:** Provision of at least two (2) cooked meals per day, supplemented by dry ration for residents who are employed or engaged in daily wage work. Special dietary requirements arising from medical conditions, pregnancy, lactation, or age shall be accommodated wherever practicable.
3. **Health and Medical Support:** Referral linkages with municipal hospitals, primary health centres, and private charitable clinics for outpatient care, maternal and child health services, and mental health counselling. Each shelter shall maintain a first-aid kit and a register of medical referrals.
4. **Sanitation and Hygiene:** Provision of clean drinking water, functional toilets, bathing facilities, and supplies of soap, sanitary pads, and other hygiene essentials. Shelters shall maintain a daily cleaning schedule and a weekly pest-control roster.
5. **Livelihood Assistance:** Facilitation of access to government employment schemes, skill-training programmes, and job placements through partnerships with vocational training institutes and employers. The Network shall maintain a job-seeker register at each shelter.
6. **Legal and Documentation Support:** Assistance with obtaining ration cards, Aadhaar cards, voter identification, caste certificates, and other essential documents. The Network shall also provide referrals for legal aid in matters of tenancy, domestic violence, and child custody.
7. **Education and Childcare:** Arrangement of non-formal education, remedial classes, and recreational activities for children residing in shelters, in coordination with local schools and non-governmental organisations.
8. **Psychosocial Support:** Provision of group counselling, individual grief support, and crisis intervention services, delivered by trained social workers or counsellors, either as staff or as empanelled volunteers.
**AASHRAYA EMERGENCY SHELTER NETWORK**
**FOUNDING CHARTER (CONTINUED)**

---

**ARTICLE V: GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE**

**5.1 General Body.** The General Body of the Network shall consist of all founding members, life members, and such ordinary members as may be admitted from time to time in accordance with the Bye-Laws. The General Body shall meet at least once in every calendar year, ordinarily during the month of June, and shall be the supreme authority of the Network. Notice of every General Body meeting shall be sent to members at least fifteen (15) days in advance, specifying the agenda, date, time, and venue.

**5.2 Governing Board.** The affairs of the Network shall be managed and supervised by a Governing Board consisting of not less than seven (7) and not more than eleven (11) members. The composition of the Governing Board shall be as follows:

(a) President – one (1);
(b) Vice-President – one (1);
(c) Secretary – one (1);
(d) Treasurer – one (1);
(e) Joint Secretary – one (1); and
(f) Executive Members – not less than two (2) and not more than six (6).

The Governing Board shall be elected by the General Body at its Annual General Meeting for a term of three (3) years. No member shall hold the office of President for more than two (2) consecutive terms.

**5.3 Powers and Duties of the Governing Board.** The Governing Board shall have the following powers and duties:

1. To formulate, review, and approve policies, programmes, and budgets for the Network.
2. To approve the opening, closure, or relocation of any shelter or project.
3. To appoint, suspend, or remove staff of the Network, other than staff appointed by the General Body.
4. To enter into agreements, memoranda of understanding, and contracts on behalf of the Network, subject to the provisions of this Charter.
5. To constitute committees, sub-committees, or task forces for specific purposes, and to delegate such powers as may be necessary.
6. To approve the annual audited accounts and the annual report for presentation to the General Body.
7. To ensure compliance with all applicable laws, rules, regulations, and the terms of this Charter.
8. To perform such other acts as may be necessary for the achievement of the objectives of the Network, not inconsistent with this Charter or the laws in force.

**5.4 Meetings of the Governing Board.** The Governing Board shall meet at least once in every quarter, and in any case not less than four (4) times in a calendar year. The Secretary shall convene the meetings by giving not less than seven (7) days’ written notice, unless a shorter notice is agreed to by a majority of the members. The quorum for a meeting of the Governing Board shall be one-third of the total number of members, or five (5), whichever is less. Decisions shall ordinarily be taken by consensus, and where a vote is required, by a simple majority of members present and voting. The President shall have a casting vote in the event of a tie.

**5.5 Office Bearers: Duties and Responsibilities.**

(a) *President*: The President shall preside over all meetings of the General Body and the Governing Board, shall supervise the overall functioning of the Network, and shall represent the Network in its dealings with government authorities, donors, and the public. The President shall have the power to authenticate the minutes of meetings and other official documents.

(b) *Vice-President*: The Vice-President shall assist the President and shall perform the duties of the President in the latter’s absence or incapacity.
**ARTICLE VI: AMENDMENTS**

**6.1 Power to Amend.** This Charter may be amended, in whole or in part, by a resolution passed by a two-thirds (2/3) majority of the members of the General Body present and voting at a meeting duly convened for the purpose, provided that the proposed amendment has been circulated in writing to all members not less than twenty-one (21) days prior to the date of such meeting.

**6.2 Restrictions on Amendment.** No amendment shall be made which would:
(a) alter the objectives of the Network as set out in Article II, except to the extent necessary to comply with the provisions of any law in force;
(b) divert or permit the diversion of the assets or income of the Network, directly or indirectly, to any person or entity other than in furtherance of the objectives of the Network;
(c) amend the provisions of this Article VI, except by a resolution passed by a three-fourths (3/4) majority of the members of the General Body present and voting.

**6.3 Registration and Approval.** Any amendment duly passed shall take effect from the date of its passage by the General Body, provided that where such amendment requires the prior approval or subsequent intimation of any statutory authority, including the Registrar of Societies or the Commissioner of Income Tax, the same shall be obtained or given, as the case may be, within the time prescribed by law. The Secretary shall be responsible for ensuring that all necessary filings are made in a timely manner.

**6.4 Record of Amendments.** All amendments shall be recorded in a separate register maintained for the purpose, which shall be signed by the President and the Secretary. The register shall contain the text of the original provision, the text of the amended provision, the date of the resolution, and the names of the members who moved and seconded the resolution.

**ARTICLE VII: RATIFICATION AND COMMENCEMENT**

**7.1 Adoption.** This Charter was adopted by the founding members of the Aashraya Emergency Shelter Network at a meeting held on 2015-04-01 at the office of the Network, located at 14/B, Lake View Road, Ward 9, Bhubaneswar, Odisha.

**7.3 Commencement.** This Charter shall come into force with immediate effect from the date of its adoption, i.e., 2015-04-01. All activities of the Network, including the opening of bank accounts, the appointment of staff, and the commencement of shelter operations, shall be undertaken in accordance with the provisions of this Charter.

documents.content:
1. **Dignity First:** All services shall be delivered in a manner that respects the inherent dignity and privacy of every guest. No individual shall be turned away from an AESN facility solely due to lack of documentation or identification.

2. **Temporary Bridge:** Shelters operated by the Network are intended as a temporary bridge, typically not exceeding ninety (90) days, during which guests are connected to long-term housing solutions, vocational training, or family reunification services.

3. **Safety and Security:** Every facility shall maintain a secure environment with 24/7 staffing, controlled entry, and a zero-tolerance policy for violence, theft, substance abuse on premises, or harassment.

4. **Non-Refoulement:** No guest shall be forcibly transferred to another facility or returned to a hazardous situation without a documented alternative plan agreed upon by the guest and a case manager.

5. **Transparency:** All financial transactions, donor contributions, and expenditure records shall be maintained in an auditable manner and made available to the Board of Directors and relevant regulatory authorities upon request.

6. **Collaboration:** The Network shall actively coordinate with government bodies, local law enforcement, healthcare providers, and other non-governmental organizations to ensure comprehensive support for guests.

---

**ARTICLE III: GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE**

**Section 3.1: Board of Directors**

The affairs of the Network shall be managed by a Board of Directors comprising not less than five (5) and not more than nine (9) members. The initial Board of Directors, as of 2015-04-01, is constituted as follows:

The founding charter records that Aashraya Emergency Shelter Network was established on 2015-04-01. Record status: historical.

**Section 3.2: Terms and Meetings**

- Board members shall serve a term of three (3) years, renewable by mutual consent.
- The Board shall convene at least once per quarter. A simple majority shall constitute a quorum.
- Day-to-day operational decisions may be delegated to the Executive Director, who shall report to the Board.

**Section 3.3: Executive Director**

The Executive Director shall be appointed by the Board and shall be responsible for:
- Overseeing all shelter operations and staff.
- Implementing Board policies.
- Managing donor relations and fundraising.
- Ensuring compliance with all applicable local, state, and central regulations.

---

**ARTICLE IV: OPERATIONAL SCOPE**

**Section 4.1: Types of Facilities**

AESN may operate, either directly or in partnership, the following types of facilities:
- **Emergency Night Shelters:** Open year-round, providing overnight accommodation and morning meals.
- **Family Transition Shelters:** Private or semi-private rooms for families with children, with access to communal kitchen and laundry facilities.
- **Disaster Response Camps:** Temporary structures set up in the immediate aftermath of a natural calamity, in coordination with the Karnataka State Disaster Management Authority.

**Section 5.3: Staffing Norms**

- Each emergency night shelter shall have a minimum of two (2) staff members on duty during operational hours.
- A caretaker shall be present on the premises at all times.
- Volunteers may supplement staff, but shall not replace paid positions.
- All staff shall undergo a background verification prior to appointment.

**Section 5.4: Grievance Redressal**

A Grievance Redressal Committee shall be constituted at the headquarters in Mumbai. The Committee shall:
- Receive complaints from beneficiaries, staff, or the public.
- Acknowledge receipt of a complaint within three (3) working days.
- Resolve the complaint within thirty (30) days of receipt.
- Maintain a register of complaints and their resolutions.

---

**ARTICLE VI: FINANCIAL PROVISIONS**

**Section 6.1: Sources of Funding**

The Network may raise funds through:
- Grants from central and state government schemes, including the National Urban Livelihoods Mission and state-level homelessness programs.
- Donations from individuals, trusts, and corporations.
- Corporate social responsibility contributions.
- Income from lawful activities, including the sale of recycled materials.

**Section 6.2: Utilization of Funds**

Funds shall be utilized for:
- Operational expenses, including rent, utilities, and staff salaries.
- Procurement of food, bedding, and hygiene supplies.
- Maintenance and minor repairs of facilities.
- Training and capacity-building of staff.
- Contingency reserves for disaster response.

**Section 6.3: Auditing**

- The accounts of the Network shall be audited annually by a chartered accountant appointed by the Board.
- The audited financial statements shall be presented to the Board within six (6) months of the close of the financial year.
- A copy of the audited statements shall be made available to donors and regulatory authorities upon request.

---

**ARTICLE VII: AMENDMENTS**

According to the administrative records, Aashraya Emergency Shelter Network has headquarters in Mumbai. Record status: current.

**Section 7.1: Procedure for Amendment**

This charter may be amended by a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority of the Board members present and voting, provided that:
- Notice of the proposed amendment is circulated at least fifteen (15) days prior to the meeting.
- The amendment is consistent with the objectives of the Network and applicable law.

**Section 7.2: Record of Amendments**

All amendments shall be recorded in a separate register maintained at the headquarters in Mumbai, with the date of amendment and the names of the Board members voting in favour.

---

**ARTICLE VIII: DISSOLUTION**

**Section 8.1: Dissolution Procedure**

The Network may be dissolved by a resolution passed by a three-fourths majority of the total Board membership. Upon dissolution:
- All debts and liabilities shall be settled.
- Remaining assets shall be transferred to another organization with similar objectives, as decided by the Board.
- A final report shall be submitted to the Registrar of Societies.

---

**Section 8.2: Effective Date**

This charter shall take effect from the date of its adoption, as recorded in the minutes of the founding meeting.

---

**CERTIFICATION**

We, the undersigned, being the founding members of Aashraya Emergency Shelter Network, hereby certify that the above constitutes the true and complete charter of the Network, adopted on this day, 2015-04-01.

**SECTION 9: OPERATIONAL SCOPE AND SERVICE AREAS**

**Section 9.1: Primary Service Areas**

The Network shall operate emergency shelters and allied services within the following administrative regions, subject to the availability of resources and the execution of memoranda of understanding with local authorities:

1. Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR), including the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai, Thane Municipal Corporation, Navi Mumbai Municipal Corporation, and the Panvel Municipal Corporation.
2. Pune Metropolitan Region, including the Pune Municipal Corporation and Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation.
3. Nagpur Municipal Corporation.
4. Nashik Municipal Corporation.
5. Aurangabad Municipal Corporation.
6. Such other districts or municipal areas as the Board may designate by resolution from time to time.

The Board may, upon recommendation of the Executive Director, temporarily extend operations beyond the above areas in response to a declared disaster, a public health emergency, or a mass displacement event, provided that such extension is documented and reported to the Board at its next meeting.

**Section 9.2: Nature of Services**

The Network shall provide, or facilitate through partner agencies, the following categories of services:

1. **Emergency Shelter:** Provision of temporary, safe, and dignified accommodation for individuals and families rendered homeless due to disaster, fire, eviction, domestic violence, or other crises. Shelter facilities shall be operated on a twenty-four-hour basis and shall include separate dormitories for men, women, and families, with due regard for privacy and safety.
2. **Food and Nutrition:** Provision of at least two (2) cooked meals per day, supplemented by dry ration for residents who are employed or engaged in daily wage work. Special dietary requirements arising from medical conditions, pregnancy, lactation, or age shall be accommodated wherever practicable.
3. **Health and Medical Support:** Referral linkages with municipal hospitals, primary health centres, and private charitable clinics for outpatient care, maternal and child health services, and mental health counselling. Each shelter shall maintain a first-aid kit and a register of medical referrals.
4. **Sanitation and Hygiene:** Provision of clean drinking water, functional toilets, bathing facilities, and supplies of soap, sanitary pads, and other hygiene essentials. Shelters shall maintain a daily cleaning schedule and a weekly pest-control roster.
5. **Livelihood Assistance:** Facilitation of access to government employment schemes, skill-training programmes, and job placements through partnerships with vocational training institutes and employers. The Network shall maintain a job-seeker register at each shelter.
6. **Legal and Documentation Support:** Assistance with obtaining ration cards, Aadhaar cards, voter identification, caste certificates, and other essential documents. The Network shall also provide referrals for legal aid in matters of tenancy, domestic violence, and child custody.
7. **Education and Childcare:** Arrangement of non-formal education, remedial classes, and recreational activities for children residing in shelters, in coordination with local schools and non-governmental organisations.
8. **Psychosocial Support:** Provision of group counselling, individual grief support, and crisis intervention services, delivered by trained social workers or counsellors, either as staff or as empanelled volunteers.

The General Body shall meet at least once in every calendar year, ordinarily during the month of June, and shall be the supreme authority of the Network. Notice of every General Body meeting shall be sent to members at least fifteen (15) days in advance, specifying the agenda, date, time, and venue.

**5.2 Governing Board.** The affairs of the Network shall be managed and supervised by a Governing Board consisting of not less than seven (7) and not more than eleven (11) members. The composition of the Governing Board shall be as follows:

(a) President – one (1);
(b) Vice-President – one (1);
(c) Secretary – one (1);
(d) Treasurer – one (1);
(e) Joint Secretary – one (1); and
(f) Executive Members – not less than two (2) and not more than six (6).

The Governing Board shall be elected by the General Body at its Annual General Meeting for a term of three (3) years. No member shall hold the office of President for more than two (2) consecutive terms.

**5.3 Powers and Duties of the Governing Board.** The Governing Board shall have the following powers and duties:

1. To formulate, review, and approve policies, programmes, and budgets for the Network.
2. To approve the opening, closure, or relocation of any shelter or project.
3. To appoint, suspend, or remove staff of the Network, other than staff appointed by the General Body.
4. To enter into agreements, memoranda of understanding, and contracts on behalf of the Network, subject to the provisions of this Charter.
5. To constitute committees, sub-committees, or task forces for specific purposes, and to delegate such powers as may be necessary.
6. To approve the annual audited accounts and the annual report for presentation to the General Body.
7. To ensure compliance with all applicable laws, rules, regulations, and the terms of this Charter.
8. To perform such other acts as may be necessary for the achievement of the objectives of the Network, not inconsistent with this Charter or the laws in force.

**5.4 Meetings of the Governing Board.** The Governing Board shall meet at least once in every quarter, and in any case not less than four (4) times in a calendar year. The Secretary shall convene the meetings by giving not less than seven (7) days’ written notice, unless a shorter notice is agreed to by a majority of the members. The quorum for a meeting of the Governing Board shall be one-third of the total number of members, or five (5), whichever is less. Decisions shall ordinarily be taken by consensus, and where a vote is required, by a simple majority of members present and voting. The President shall have a casting vote in the event of a tie.

**5.5 Office Bearers: Duties and Responsibilities.**

(a) *President*: The President shall preside over all meetings of the General Body and the Governing Board, shall supervise the overall functioning of the Network, and shall represent the Network in its dealings with government authorities, donors, and the public. The President shall have the power to authenticate the minutes of meetings and other official documents.

(b) *Vice-President*: The Vice-President shall assist the President and shall perform the duties of the President in the latter’s absence or incapacity.

**ARTICLE VI: AMENDMENTS**

**6.1 Power to Amend.** This Charter may be amended, in whole or in part, by a resolution passed by a two-thirds (2/3) majority of the members of the General Body present and voting at a meeting duly convened for the purpose, provided that the proposed amendment has been circulated in writing to all members not less than twenty-one (21) days prior to the date of such meeting.

**6.2 Restrictions on Amendment.** No amendment shall be made which would:
(a) alter the objectives of the Network as set out in Article II, except to the extent necessary to comply with the provisions of any law in force;
(b) divert or permit the diversion of the assets or income of the Network, directly or indirectly, to any person or entity other than in furtherance of the objectives of the Network;
(c) amend the provisions of this Article VI, except by a resolution passed by a three-fourths (3/4) majority of the members of the General Body present and voting.

**6.3 Registration and Approval.** Any amendment duly passed shall take effect from the date of its passage by the General Body, provided that where such amendment requires the prior approval or subsequent intimation of any statutory authority, including the Registrar of Societies or the Commissioner of Income Tax, the same shall be obtained or given, as the case may be, within the time prescribed by law. The Secretary shall be responsible for ensuring that all necessary filings are made in a timely manner.

**6.4 Record of Amendments.** All amendments shall be recorded in a separate register maintained for the purpose, which shall be signed by the President and the Secretary. The register shall contain the text of the original provision, the text of the amended provision, the date of the resolution, and the names of the members who moved and seconded the resolution.
